Subject: Multiparametric MRI of the Prostate | Institution: Ziekenhuis Gelderse Vallei, Ede | Date: 15 January 2025

Clinical indication: Assessment of an elevated prostate-specific antigen level of 4.2 ng/mL alongside a history of a previously positive biopsy.

FINDINGS:
The gland measures 69.0 mL. High b-value DWI sequences highlight marked restricted diffusion, corroborated by correspondingly low ADC values, within a focal hypointense abnormality measuring roughly 18 x 15 x 12 mm situated at the mid-gland level of the right peripheral zone. Dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging captures early, focal enhancement. The neurovascular bundles remain intact. No definitive extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle invasion is apparent. The bladder and rectum demonstrate normal imaging characteristics.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 5 lesion in the right mid-peripheral zone. Prostate volume 69.0 mL. PSAD 0.06 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.81166416.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: A December 2023 reading of 3.0 ng/mL triggered a follow-up test to monitor the rising trend. The patient received lifestyle guidance, with documentation noting a 4.0 ng/mL assessment threshold.

previous_notes.author: Dr. R. Visser (GP)
previous_notes.text: An initial measurement of 2.5 ng/mL sparked a differential between benign enlargement and early malignancy. A subsequent PSA check was booked for mid-2024, coinciding with standard health screenings.
